title: Northern Ireland
summary: Northern Ireland experienced decades of sectarian conflict known as "The Troubles" (late 1960s–1998). The 1998 Good Friday Agreement substantially reduced large-scale violence; ongoing community-level reconciliation, cross-community programs, and support for victims are part of continuing peace-building efforts.

initiatives.name: Community Relations Council (CRC)
initiatives.description: Supports peace-building projects across Northern Ireland, offering grants and research into reconciliation.

initiatives.name: Corrymeela Community
initiatives.description: Northern Ireland's longest-running peace and reconciliation charity, running residential and community programs to promote contact and understanding.

initiatives.name: WAVE Trauma Centre
initiatives.description: Provides trauma counselling and support services to victims of the conflict, contributing to community recovery.
